newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan settles Canadian lawsuit, plans new smelter.
newsitem.headline: Alcan settles Canadian lawsuit, plans new smelter.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd. ( ) on Tuesday settled a lawsuit against the British Columbia government over its canceled Kemano hydroelectric project and said it plans to build a C$1.2 billion ($876 million) smelter at Kitimat, British Columbia.

Subject to economic and market conditions, the new smelter could be operational as early as Jan. 1, 2003 and no later than Jan. 1, 2010, the Montreal-based company said. Under terms of the settlement, Alcan agreed to restart idle capacity at its existing Kitimat smelter and bring it up to full capacity by Jan. 1, 1998.

Alcan said the agreement signals the end of its court action, in which it sought damages for losses incurred at its half-completed Kemano Completion Project, cancelled by the province in January 1995.
Alcan wrote off its $420 million investment in Kemano in the third quarter of 1995 and subsequently sued the British Columbia government.
The settlement provides for a power replacement option that will allow Alcan to expand its British Columbia operations while maintaining the company's existing power sales agreement with B.C. Hydro.

Alcan said more than 90 percent of the aluminum made at its 272,000-metric-ton Kitimat smelter is exported to the Asia Pacific region. The Kitimat smelter has 22,000 metric tons of idle capacity, a company spokeswoman said.
